newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania passes law to allow foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Albania passes law to allow foreign investment.

text.p: Albania will allow foreigners to trade and invest in privatisation vouchers in enterprises the Balkan nation is selling off, the deputy minister of the newly-created Privatisation Ministry said on Wednesday.
"The law now allows citizens from every part of the world to buy privatisation vouchers and use them to buy into assets being privatised," Uran Veseshta told a news conference.
He added the law, announced on Wednesday but passed last week, would formalise what was already common practice in Albania, and that it would make the process more transparent and less bureaucratic.
Foreigners originally bought vouchers through registered Albanian companies but now they can buy them directly.

Veseshta told reporters the privatisation ministry, set up in the second term of the Democratic Party cabinet of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi, was created to provide a more efficient, functional and smoother privatisation scheme.
He added his ministry, which manages the state's property, representative of its property, was now empowered to conduct the entire privatisation process.
Albania is committed to pressing ahead with the privatisation of key industries, notably in oil, mining and public utilities, Veseshta said.
